incident-bot: ALERT: Hawthorne dedicated pool — unusual token delta observed vs. metering baseline. Paging oncall. Severity: P2. Affected: hawthorne-prod (dedicated-3), potential billing impact. Please ack and triage.

Maya (oncall): acked. pinging infra and billing. any initial context?

Jordan P.: I see a spike in generated token counts from the serving logs starting 1908754000 — roughly +18% over baseline for the last 12m. Not seeing corresponding traffic increase at the API gateway.

Samira K.: @Maya can you confirm customer report? Harper (AE) — did Hawthorne flag anything on their side?

Harper (AE): customer noticed unexpected invoice preview delta in last 24h and opened a ticket. They said no app changes. Sending the customer ticket id: HW-9812.

Ria Ops: running quick check on metering service. If metering consumer is replaying events we could double-count tokens. Starting a tail on the meter consumer logs for hawthorne-tenant id = hawthorne-123.

Eli (infra): I see a pattern: between 1908753900 and 1908754100 one of the dedicated pool GPUs (dedicated-3-node-2) restarted due to OOM and we had 2x warm restarts of the model backend. Might be KV cache repopulation causing duplicate token emission to the metering pipeline.

Maya (oncall): mitigation path? Can we temporarily throttle or pin model variant to avoid double-inference while we investigate?

Jordan P.: We can toggle routing for hawthorne-123 to the canary-less variant (model-2b-static) to avoid hot cache warmups. Command to route tenant inline (internal tool):

```
# route-ctl set-route --tenant hawthorne-123 --pool dedicated-3 --model model-2b-static --force
```

Samira K.: Doing the routing now. Expecting a short reconnect for open sessions (~10s).

incident-bot: ACTION: Routing change executed by Samira K. at 1908754360.

Harper (AE): I notified the customer about a mitigation change — they approved temporary routing. They're asking for a timeline on reconciliation.

Ria Ops: while routing change reduces replay surface, we still need to reconcile tokens already counted. I'll pull the metering offsets and raw event ids for hawthorne-123. SQL snippet I'll run against metering DB:

```
SELECT event_id, token_count, created_at, source FROM metering.events
WHERE tenant_id = 'hawthorne-123' AND created_at >= to_timestamp(1908753600)
ORDER BY created_at;
```

Eli (infra): adding: check the serving runtime logs for duplicate request ids. I found entries where request_id was retried by the autoscaler: `req-8f3b` appears 3 times with identical input and token output, timestamps 1908753912, 1908753970, 1908754025. That aligns with the OOM restart window.

Jordan P.: If meter events are emitted per successful completion, retries might have been emitted multiple times before idempotency filter processed them. Metering consumer has recent change to async acking — might have allowed duplicates when backend reconnected.

Maya (oncall): ok. Steps: 1) keep routing to static model (done), 2) run metering dedupe job for event_id duplicates, 3) produce reconciliation report for billing and customer. Who owns 2/3?

Ria Ops: I'll own the dedupe query and produce a CSV of suspect event_ids + token sums. ETA 30m.

BillingBot: Noted. We'll hold automated invoice runs for hawthorne-123 until reconciliation complete. Marking account on billing-hold flag.

Harper (AE): Please include the customer-facing summary once you have numbers — they want the diff and a proposed credit if overcharge confirmed.

Samira K.: running the dedupe query now. Quick preview: dedupe will remove events with duplicated `request_id` where identical token_count and within a 2-minute window. Example output (sanitized):

```
request_id, occurrences, total_tokens_counted, deduped_tokens
req-8f3b, 3, 15000, 5000
req-9c2a, 2, 9800, 4900
```

Maya (oncall): good. After dedupe, please also regenerate per-hour token series for the last 48h so billing can see corrected usage curve.

Ria Ops: CSV generated: /internal/ops/recon/hawthorne-123/1908754321-dedupe.csv. Summary: approx 14.6% of tokens in the spike window appear duplicated — raw counted tokens 2,156,000 -> deduped 1,876,200. I'll drop a reconciliation report in 20m.

incident-bot: NOTE: Hawthorne account put on billing_hold by BillingBot at 1908754520.

BillingBot: prepping a provisional credit calc. ETA 45m after recon report.

Jordan P.: Logging followups: file a post-incident ticket to root cause: autoscaler OOM -> backend restarts -> meter duplicate emission -> metering consumer async ack regression. Also add a mitigation: make metering events idempotent at ingestion (de-dup by request_id) rather than relying on later batch dedupe.

Eli (infra): filing infra followup RFC. Also will add a guard to reduce retry emission during backend warmups.

Harper (AE): Customer update: they want confirmation that charges will be adjusted and not retried invoiced. I told them we're holding billing and will share report.

Samira K.: final note: the routing change removed the ongoing spike within ~2 minutes. No further duplicate request_ids seen after 1908754380.

Maya (oncall): thanks team. Next: Ria deliver recon report, Billing produce credit, infra + eng create postmortem and mitigation tickets. I'll hand this to oncall rotation SREs for next 24h monitoring. Closing the live page in 10m if no new anomalies. :thumbsup:

Incident summary (automated):
- Customer: Hawthorne (tenant hawthorne-123)
- Impact: inflated token counts in metering pipeline due to duplicated request emissions during backend restarts (~14.6% overcount in spike window)
- Immediate mitigation: route hawthorne to model-2b-static to avoid warmup replays; billing_hold applied
- Next steps: metering dedupe + reconciliation CSV, billing credit calc, infra/eng postmortem.

Harper (AE): customer acknowledged and appreciated the rapid response. Keeping them in the loop.

Maya (oncall): closing live coord — will update thread after recon and credit applied.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED for live paging at 1908754987 (auto-archive).
